notes: Company background: mid-market B2B SaaS — user-help center + in-app assistant product; heavy doc-search traffic during business hours.
Why Redwood: performance + ability to move from Hosted -> Dedicated without changing SDKs; strong cost levers (batching/quantize) attractive.
Primary ask: replicate production traffic profile in POC; validate 99th percentile latency <= 120ms for short assistant prompts, sustained throughput ~250 qps during peak.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, use customer KMS for keys, and keep EU customer data in eu-west region. Legal requires audit log retention 1 year.
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable latency spikes during support surges; can't have models degrade mid-day.'
Commercial: leaning hosted initially for dev velocity but want Dedicated for predictable cost and isolation once POC succeeds.
Pricing sensitivity: target ARR band $50k-150k; needs clearer Dedicated commit tiers and overage behavior.
POC constraints: VPC peering + firewall rules must be verified before canary start; infra team requires runbook and rollback playbook.
Reference artifacts: security deck reviewed (drive link), demo recording in Fireflies (ff_20241020_demosession_v2).
Internal stakeholders: Product Lead (Alyssa Chen), CTO (Marcus Delaunay), Infra Lead (Ravi Patel), Procurement (Lina Gomez).
requirements_summary: Workloads: chat-first assistant, doc-search embedding recall, nightly summarization jobs
Latency SLOs: p99 <= 120ms for short assistant prompts (<=256 tokens), tail latency control important
Throughput: average 80 qps, burst to 250 qps during business hours; sustained token throughput budgeted
Model preferences: prefer curated open models; want ability to use quantized variants for cost vs fp16 for quality
Routing needs: regional routing (na/eu) + fallback to alternate model variant during capacity constraints
Observability: per-request token cost breakdown, traces, and alerting on quality regressions
poc_plan: Phase 0 (pre-POC): network sign-off, KMS test, legal template review — target complete by 2024-11-20
Phase 1 (2-week canary): deploy Dedicated to 2 GPU nodes in na-east, route 5% of traffic from Hosted -> Dedicated; monitor latency, cost, and errors
Phase 1 checks: p99 latency, end-to-end request tracing, KV-cache hit rates, token-cost per route
Canary rollout strategy: start with internal beta -> 5% production -> 20% -> 50% (if OK) -> scale
Fallback routing plan: primary route = Dedicated (preferred variant: quantized 4-bit), fallback order = Hosted (fp16 better quality) -> alternate region (eu-west) -> rollback to Hosted full
Model variant rules: prefer quantized variant for cost under normal load; auto-fallback to higher-precision when quality threshold fails or latency spikes
Region failover: automated route to eu-west with sticky session awareness; DR test scheduled during POC week 2
Rollback playbook: immediate traffic reroute to Hosted API if p99 > 250ms or error rate > 1% sustained for 5m
Success criteria: stability at 50% traffic with p99 <= 120ms and token-cost within projected band; signed procurement to follow
